ideas.label: French Defence
ideas.principle: Attack the base of the opposing pawn chain.
ideas.summary: The French Defence creates a locked or semi-locked center in which each side attacks a pawn chain. White usually has more kingside space; Black develops counterplay against d4 with ...c5 and later challenges e5 with ...f6.

ideas.label: French Defence
ideas.principle: Improve the bad bishop while attacking the center.
ideas.summary: French Defence strategy revolves around Black's light-squared bishop and timely pawn breaks. Black should not accept permanent passivity: improve the bishop through d7-e8-g6, b7-a6, or a later ...b6, and coordinate this with pressure on d4.
games: Naidon, Pietro Weber vs Born, Ary 2026 (C00)
Eslava Cordoba, Salome vs Rodriguez Patino, Santiago 2026 (C00)

ideas.label: French Defence
ideas.principle: Use a closed center to transfer forces toward the king.
ideas.summary: In the French Advance, White can support a kingside attack with f4-f5, queen pressure on h5, and rook lifts along the third rank. These attacking ideas work best while the center stays closed; if Black breaks with ...f6 at the right moment, White's advanced e5-pawn can become a target.
games: Naidon, Pietro Weber vs Born, Ary 2026 (C00)
Eslava Cordoba, Salome vs Rodriguez Patino, Santiago 2026 (C00)

ideas.label: French Defence
ideas.principle: Judge an isolated pawn by its activity, not only its weakness.
ideas.summary: When the French center transforms into an isolated d-pawn position, blockading d5 is not automatically enough. The defender must control the pawn's advance and the active squares behind it; exchanges favor the blockader only when they reduce the isolated pawn's dynamic support.
games: Naidon, Pietro Weber vs Born, Ary 2026 (C00)
